title: Capability ledger: one row per mode a user could believe exists, with the proof behind it
description: Read and written by expectrail.capabilities; the instance is docs/capabilities.json and docs/capabilities.md is rendered from it. A row's status says how far the mode is proven, its grade says what kind of evidence its best recorded run produced, and every row links the test, record or CI run that shows it. A measured row needs a CI run link, and every run link carries the run's conclusion as read when the row was written. The schema checks shape; expectrail.capabilities.problems checks the rules a schema cannot (links that resolve, files that exist, what the README and the site advertise).

field.description: One whole field of a notice's message: no semicolon, no line break, no space at either end.

member.description: The value of one member of a JSON notice. 1.0 is not a whole number here: `python3 -m expectrail.capabilities check` refuses it.

count.description: One count tied to a run's notices (the annotations a job writes with ::notice). With `count`: `of` is how many notices have a title matching `titled`, and `n` is how many of those have `count` as one whole field of their message; every one of those notices must have `count` or `otherwise`, once and not both, or the count cannot be told. With `reads`: exactly one notice has the title and one of its fields is `reads` with {n} and {of} filled in. A message's fields are what lies between its semicolons. With `has`: every notice with the title is one JSON object; `of` is how many have the members under `where` as given (all of them, without `where`), and `n` is how many of those have the members under `has` as given. Words in `says` that hold no count speak of every notice counted, so `n` must be `of`; the check holds that.

says.description: The words in `shows` this entry backs, for example "8 of 8". When they hold a count it must be `n` of `of`.

titled.description: A notice's whole title; * stands for any text and nothing else is special.

not.description: Titles left out of those `titled` matches, written the same way.

count.description: The field a notice must have, whole, to be counted in `n`.

otherwise.description: With `count`: the field a notice that is not counted in `n` must have instead, for example "caught with SAM off: no" beside "caught with SAM off: yes". Required whenever `n` is less than `of`; a schema cannot compare two numbers, so `python3 -m expectrail.capabilities check` and the test suite hold that. Without it every notice must have `count`.

reads.description: The field the one notice must have, with {n} and {of} where the numbers go. Neither may stand right beside a digit or beside the other: "{n}{of}" would be filled the same by 1 of 11 and by 11 of 1.

has.description: For notices whose message is one JSON object: the members a notice must have, each equal to the value given, to be counted in `n`. Every notice counted in `of` must have each of these members with a value of the same kind (true or false, a whole number, text), or the count cannot be told.

where.description: With `has`: the members a notice with the title must have, each equal to the value given or to one of a list of values, to be counted in `of`. Every notice with the title must have each of these members with a value of the same kind, or the count cannot be told.

kind.description: run: a CI run on GitHub, by URL. test: a test file in this repository. record: a file in this repository written from a run's output, or a page that lists its runs.

conclusion.description: For a run: how the run ended, as GitHub's API reported it when the row was written. A recorded value; `python3 -m expectrail.capabilities recheck` reads it again and reports a difference.

jobs.description: For a run: the names of the jobs this evidence rests on, as GitHub lists them. `recheck` fails when one is not in the run or did not end in success. Left out, only the run's conclusion is held to.

counts.description: For a run: the counts in `shows` that are tied to the notices the run published. `recheck` reads the notices of the run's jobs and counts again. A count in `shows` with no entry here is as its writer wrote it.

conclusionNote.description: Required when a cited run did not end in success: why it is evidence all the same. Only an implemented or experimental row may cite such a run.

profile.description: The engine or kind of software, and the platform it has run on.

observer.description: What looks at the run: the engine's record, a vision model, a page's layout boxes, or none.

entryPoints.description: Python modules a person runs with python3 -m, or that hold the mode. Each must exist.

names.description: Names the README or the site uses for this mode's engine, model or agent.

limits.description: What the evidence does not show, in a sentence.

phases.description: The same seconds split by phase, copied from the run's timing.json (expectrail.verify-timing/v1). They add up to seconds.

phasesFrom.description: Where in the run the phases can be read.

notModes.description: Things the README or the site names that are not modes, each with the reason.

nameWatch.description: Engine, model and agent names. If the README or the site uses one, a row must list it under names.
